topics.label: Course Welcome and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Pathogen and Damage Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system detects infections and cellular injury by recognizing conserved molecular patterns while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families, Signaling, and Inflammasomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the major pattern recognition receptor families, their intracellular signaling cascades, and the assembly and regulation of the inflammasome.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Complications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells coordinate leukocyte extravasation into inflamed tissues and lymphatic drainage, as well as the life-threatening risks of uncontrolled systemic activation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that resolve inflammation, restore tissue integrity, and form granulomas when infections persist.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and announces the next lecture on the complement system.
